Data: <world>/wishes/buildings.json, each child's shelf, library-copy build.json. Repro: save a building with a chain on 1.21.8, open the world on 1.21.10, rebuild or place it from the shelf. How to rebuild (a working start: commit 96881f8 on neoforge-1.21.10 for the read-time wiring and marker, .port/1.21.10/upgrade-remap-wip.patch on neoforge-1.21.10 for the journal, single-id and newer-marker parts): a versioned table (compat/BlockRenames ROWS (from, to, since)) applied when a record is read; an "mc" marker on every stored record, an unmarked record counting as 1.21.8; the file rewritten only on its next save; never a record with an older marker written over a newer file (a newer one is read-only for that run). issues.notes: Tag: upgrade-only. upgrade-only. What breaks: every CBScript pack a player wished before 1.21.11 has 'gamerule maxCommandChainLength 1000000000' in its reset function (the compiler's boilerplate). 1.21.11 replaced the camelCase game-rule names with registry ids (Mojang's GameRuleRegistryFix: max_command_sequence_length), so that line is an unknown command, and one unparseable line fails the whole function to load: the pack's state is not reset/initialised. Stored data: the installed wished packs in a world's datapacks folder and the mod's own pack store (DatapackStore). New packs compiled on 1.21.11 (moddy-cbscript mc/1.21.11) are not affected. Workaround: wish the power again on 1.21.11 (recompiles the pack). A fix would be a versioned rename on install (DatapackDialect.correctFunction), deliberately not built (owner: no upgrade-only work). Unverified: found by reading the 1.21.11 command tree and the compiler's output; not yet reproduced in a world upgraded from 1.21.10. Verify by: on 1.21.10, wish a power (any CBScript pack), save; open the world on the 1.21.11 jar; /reload and check the server log for the pack's reset function failing to parse at 'gamerule maxCommandChainLength'. (Was KI-1 on the 1.21.11 rung.)
issues.title: [upgrade-only, from 1.21.11] a datapack wished before 1.21.11 fails to load its reset function (old game-rule name)

issues.notes: Tag: upgrade-only. What breaks: 26.1 moved a dimension's saved data to dimensions/minecraft/<dim>/data/<namespace>/<path>.dat (SavedDataStorage keys files by Identifier). Mojang's own world upgrade (net.minecraft.util.filefix.fixes.DimensionStorageFileFix) moves only vanilla's files (chunks, raids, world_border, scoreboard, maps, command storage...); the mod's four files stay at <world>/data/: moddingfromamod_rules.dat (WorldRules), moddingfromamod_events.dat (EventDirector), moddingfromamod_event_designs.dat (EventDesigns) and moddingfromamod_build_ground.dat (BuildGroundJournal). On 26.1.2 the mod reads moddingfromamod/rules.dat, events.dat, event_designs.dat and build_ground.dat under dimensions/minecraft/overworld/data/, finds none, and starts empty: the world's rules, staged event designs, running events and the build-ground undo journal are gone (the old files are left untouched on disk). A fresh 26.1 world is unaffected: SavedDataPathGameTest writes and reads the stores at the new path. Not fixed (owner's rule: a player's world upgrade is not supported, see the README). A migration (move each old file to its new path on first load, or a legacy read like MMVU shared/26.1.2/java/SavedDatas) is a separate, later decision, needed before the project's own houses run 26.x. Workaround: by hand, move <world>/data/moddingfromamod_X.dat to <world>/dimensions/minecraft/overworld/data/moddingfromamod/X.dat before opening the world on 26.1.2.
